headline: LEAKED: The 4.2 Million Argent 'Tactical Horse' Deployed to Myrati
summary: Documents obtained exclusively by AVIS reveal a highly classified, and bafflingly expensive, Ministry of National Defense initiative amid the ongoing Myratian Crisis. Deep within the supplemental budget for Ex-ODU forces currently fighting Edelsteinist insurgents, a line item simply titled "Asset Procurement: Equine" accounts for a staggering 4.2 million Argents.
content:
Documents obtained exclusively by AVIS reveal a highly classified, and bafflingly expensive, Ministry of National Defense initiative amid the ongoing Myratian Crisis. Deep within the supplemental budget for Ex-ODU forces currently fighting Edelsteinist insurgents, a line item simply titled "Asset Procurement: Equine" accounts for a staggering 4.2 million Argents.

AVIS can confirm that this asset is, in fact, a horse.

According to internal memos from the logistics division, the animal was procured from a private breeder with known, direct connections to President Mandy Trottier. The documentation outlines no specific combat utility, surveillance capabilities, or logistical function for the horse. The only justification provided in the procurement filing is a handwritten note stating that the animal possesses a "very serious, tactical demeanor."

When pressed on the nature of the President's connection to the procurement, one exhausted presidential aide - speaking under strict anonymity - declined to comment on the funding, but noted that President Trottier has lately "shown signs of being a horse."

When reached for official comment, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense initially denied the existence of the animal. Upon being presented with the signed authorization forms, the spokesperson pivoted, claiming the horse was a "vital component of rural theater mobility," before abruptly ending the call.

Military sources stationed in Myrati, however, paint a different picture. "It just stands there," one Ex-ODU officer told AVIS, speaking on the condition of anonymity. "They built a reinforced, climate-controlled stable for it near the command center. We're fighting MLF insurgents in the mud, and this horse gets premium oats shipped in twice a week via armored convoy. Honestly, I think President Mandy Trottier just likes horses."

The revelation comes at a time when Caprica's government is running a deficit of 343.6 billion Argents and the national credit rating has plummeted. While the Cutter administration preaches fiscal responsibility and institutional stability, it appears 4.2 million Argents is not too steep a price for a single, serious-looking horse.

headline: AVIS Declares Its Candidates of Choice: The Only Path Forward for a Fractured Chasmia
summary: AVIS extends its full unreserved endorsement to Aldric von Reichel for the upcoming Chasmia by-election, citing a need for stable institutions following the murder of MP Richard Balls. For voters looking past their first preference, AVIS recommends sitting Prime Minister Patrick Cutter as a moderate, acceptable second option against a field that includes National Rally and a hollowed-out right.
content:
The by-election called for Chasmia on 30 June 2058 carries a weight beyond the ordinary churn of Caprican politics. Richard Balls, son of the region's former Prime Minister and its sitting MP since 2056, was murdered by loyalist forces in the Myrati home of Rachel Edelstein-Powell, a killing that closed out the bloody collapse of the Independent Rachelist bloc he had represented. Balls held Chasmia across three party banners over two decades - Liberal, Jasmine Movement, Independent Rachelist - and his death leaves the seat, and the region, without the figure who had defined it for a generation. The Rachelists will not contest the seat they once held. In their place, six names are on the ballot, and for the first time, National Rally.

AVIS does not treat this contest as one force among equals, and it will not pretend otherwise. Chasmia is a centre-right region by habit, having returned only the Jasmine Movement or Avenir Caprica since the regions were re-established, and it now faces a field crowded with candidates who offer little beyond recycled relevance or imported extremism. Michael Fairbanks, Avenir Caprica's returning nominee and a former MP for the region, represents a continuation of a right that has already had its say. Izan Canon II arrives as Jasmine Movement's late replacement after Miranda Eiland-Priestly's disqualification under CEC age rules, a substitution born of administrative necessity rather than conviction. Tricky Lindegaard runs nominally as an independent while carrying Rejuvenation Party membership undisclosed on the label. And National Rally's arrival in Chasmia, fronted by Marine Le Pen, is not a debut AVIS will greet with anything but alarm - a party whose politics have no legitimate place in a region already searching for direction after violence.

Against this field, the Social Democratic Alliance has put forward list MP Aldric von Reichel, and AVIS extends him its full and unreserved endorsement. Von Reichel represents the only candidacy in this race grounded in a coherent account of what Chasmia - and Caprica - need after Balls: institutions capable of absorbing shocks like the one that just claimed the seat, a politics that does not retreat into either the stale right or the imported hate of National Rally, and a Republic that takes seriously its obligation to the people history keeps failing. AVIS believes Chasmia's voters deserve to hear plainly: von Reichel is the candidate equal to this moment.

Where AVIS departs from reflexive party loyalty is in its second word. Should Chasmia's voters look past their first preference, Moderate Reform's Patrick Cutter - the sitting Prime Minister, contesting a seat outside his previous base at Mezata - is the only other candidate in this field AVIS can recommend in good conscience. Cutter is no ally of the Alliance's programme, and AVIS will not soften that. He is a Conservative, and the differences between his party's instincts and Social Democratic Alliance's are real. But he has governed as a moderate on the issues that matter most in a region grieving a political murder: agreeable rather than doctrinaire, reachable rather than closed, serious rather than performative. In a race that includes National Rally on one end and a hollowed-out right on the other, that distinction counts for something.

AVIS's message to Chasmia is direct. Vote first for Aldric von Reichel, whose candidacy answers this moment with substance. Where that is not the outcome, Patrick Cutter remains a figure Chasmia can send to the Caprican House without shame. The seat that Ed Balls once held, and his son held after him, deserves better than drift - and better than the politics National Rally now brings to its ballot for the first time.

headline: Mandy Trottier's Scandalous Coffee Order
summary: President Mandy Trottier's preferred drink, according to sources close to the Presidential residence, is a Pumpkin Spice Sweet Cold Coffee - extra cinnamon, cold foam, no exceptions. The detail has drawn quiet notice in circles that expect a certain austerity from the office. Trottier's public rhetoric is firmly Center-Left: talk of worker-class, labour, the sacrifices we must make for the Republic. Her order suggests other priorities. Aides describe the order as a fixture of her schedule, not an occasional indulgence. One source, speaking on condition of anonymity, noted it appears on the daily brief alongside her security detail's rotation. AVIS reached out to the President's office for comment and received none.

headline: MP von Reichel Ties the Knot With Senator Proctor in Ceremony with Higher Attendance than the Parliament
summary: Member of Parliament and AVIS founder Aldric von Reichel officially became Aldric von Reichel and Senator Mary Proctor became Mary Proctor Reichel today, in a ceremony that reportedly drew more sitting legislators than most actual parliamentary sessions this year. Guests included several high-ranking government officials, numerous MPs, and a healthy contingent of Social Democratic Alliance members, leading one attendee to joke that "if this venue collapsed, we'd need an emergency election."
content:
Member of Parliament and AVIS founder Aldric von Reichel officially became Aldric von Reichel and Senator Mary Proctor became Mary Proctor Reichel today, in a ceremony that reportedly drew more sitting legislators than most actual parliamentary sessions this year. Guests included several high-ranking government officials, numerous MPs, and a healthy contingent of Social Democratic Alliance members, leading one attendee to joke that "if this venue collapsed, we'd need an emergency election."

Von Reichel, 23, and Proctor, 43 and a sitting Senator with the Alternative Labour Party, represent something of a rare cross-party union - proof, guests noted, that bipartisanship is alive and well, at least at the altar. The nearly two-decade age gap drew a few knowing smiles among attendees, though most agreed the couple seemed entirely unbothered by the math.

The reception ran on a strict Bring Your Own Alcohol policy, a decision guests either praised as refreshingly frugal or quietly blamed for the noticeably uneven quality of toasts as the evening wore on.

Notably absent from the guest list was Proctor's son, who - being only three years younger than his new stepfather - reportedly decided that attending would raise more questions than the marriage itself already had.

Neither party has commented on whether the wedding registry included a coalition agreement.
byline: By Nadia Voss, AVIS Society Desk

headline: Former PM's Shirtless "Bit Warm Today" Post Breaks Caprik, Weather is Quite Cold Actually
summary: Former Prime Minister and current Formula One driver Kosta Piastri sent Caprik into a full-blown meltdown this afternoon after posting a shirtless photo captioned simply, "Bit warm today! ☀️." The post has since amassed 51,930 likes and several thousand comments. Meteorologists have confirmed the actual temperature in the region was a mild 19 degrees. Opposition leaders have not yet responded, reportedly because their aides are refusing to hand back their phones.
byline: By Nadia Voss, AVIS Society Desk

headline: Growth Looks Good on Paper: A Look In the Details of 2057 Economic Report
summary: The government's 2057 economic release tells two different stories. Caprica grew, with GDP up 4.1% to 5.286 trillion Argents. However, spending outpaced revenue, resulting in a deficit of 6.5% of GDP financed entirely through borrowing. This pushed debt-to-GDP to 90.31% and led rating agencies to hold Caprica's credit rating at BBB+ (stable)-the lowest rating in 57 years.

headline: Local Man Wins Lifetime Supply of Ambrosia Cola, Discovers He's Diabetic Three Days Later
summary: What began as the happiest day of Denny Okafor's life ended in what his physician described as "A joke from the universe itself." Okafor, who won the grand prize in Ambrosia Cola's "Fizz or Fortune" sweepstakes last Tuesday, was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes the following Friday. Ambrosia Cola has offered to convert the remaining 1,197 crates into store credit, which Okafor describes as "somehow worse."
byline: By Nadia Voss, AVIS Society Desk

headline: AVIS FIELD REPORT: Myrati - A Fragile Turning Point
summary: After weeks of grinding, inconclusive engagements, the rural theater in Myrati has finally produced a tangible shift in momentum. Ex-ODU troops successfully located and destroyed a major separatist ammunition cache. Meanwhile, a mass-casualty attack by the MLF on the Collective Nightclub in Central Montiablo has claimed 13 lives, including eight CIVIC employees. In the southern waters, an extensive smuggling and human trafficking network linked to Los Navegantes Del Mar has been uncovered, raising fears of connections to the MLF.
content: The full report details multiple front developments. The rural theater saw a breakthrough as Ex-ODU troops destroyed a major separatist ammo cache. In Central Montiablo, a tragic mass-casualty attack on the Collective Nightclub by the MLF resulted in 13 deaths, including 8 CIVIC employees. DCNI Al Bush addressed the nation, vowing resolve. Down south, coast guard units uncovered an extensive smuggling and human trafficking network tied to Los Navegantes Del Mar, with potential links to funding the MLF.
byline: By Elsa Rourke, AVIS Politics Desk

headline: Prime Minister Announces Disappearance of Justice Balls and MP Balls; JM Leader Found Amid Bizarre Kidnapping Claims
summary: Prime Minister Patrick Cutter has announced the sudden and unexplained disappearances of Supreme Court Justice Hugh Balls, MP Richard Balls, and Jasmin Movement leader Jasmin Bergvall. While Bergvall was later located following an unannounced trip to Moeras island, the JM (Jasmin Movement) leader has since leveled wildly unsubstantiated accusations of kidnapping and cannibalism against CIVIC Director Al Bush. The whereabouts of Justice Balls—who has known ties to the Edelsteinist movement—and MP Balls remain unknown.
content:
Prime Minister Patrick Cutter shocked the nation today with the announcement that three prominent political figures—Supreme Court Justice Hugh Balls, Member of Parliament Richard Balls, and Jasmin Movement leader Jasmin Bergvall—had vanished without a trace. The disappearances triggered an immediate nationwide search by CIVIC.

While the whereabouts of Justice Balls and MP Balls remain unknown, the situation took a surreal turn when investigators located Jasmin Bergvall. Officials confirmed that the JM (Jasmin Movement) leader had simply taken an unannounced trip around Moeras island without notifying the government.

However, Bergvall’s return was accompanied by explosive and bizarre accusations. Taking to the social media platform 'Caprik,' the JM leader posted: "Al BUSH wanted to EAT ME, so he KIDNAPPED ME and LOCKED ME in his BASEMENT. I was trapped there until I MIRACULOUSLY managed to ESCAPE!!!"

The target of these claims, Al Bush, is a Member of Parliament for the governing Moderate Reform party and currently serves as the Director of CIVIC—the very agency tasked with investigating the disappearances. Both government officials and the general public have broadly dismissed Bergvall's accusations as "ridiculous," prompting quiet, low-key speculation in political circles regarding the JM leader's current mental well-being.

Despite the safe recovery of the JM leader, serious concerns remain for Justice Hugh Balls and MP Richard Balls. The disappearance of Justice Balls is particularly alarming given his widely documented close relationship with the Edelsteinists and Dame Rachel Edelstein-Powell. With the Myratian Crisis ongoing and Edelsteinist supporters still in armed revolt following Powell's recent conviction for provocation of violence, investigators are racing to determine if the missing Justice is connected to the insurrection.
byline: By Elsa Rourke, AVIS Politics Desk

headline: City Council Declares War on Potholes; Potholes Respond With Aggressive Expansion
summary: Following a bold declaration by the Mayor to eradicate all potholes by the end of the fiscal year, local asphalt anomalies seem to have taken the threat personally. A rapid overnight expansion on 4th Avenue has effectively consumed a small sedan. The Mayor's office insists the situation is under control, urging citizens to simply "drive better."
byline: By Nadia Voss, AVIS Society Desk

headline: Vote of No Confidence from Jasmin Movement Shattered in the Parliament
summary: A motion of no confidence requested by George Miliband of the Jasmin Movement was swiftly dismantled on the floor today. Parliament, including members of the opposition, voiced significant support for Prime Minister Patrick Cutter, likely citing the critical need for stability during the ongoing Myratian Crisis. Further complicating the motion, the Jasmin Movement itself appeared fractured; party chairman Jasmin was observed voting in favor of the government, severely undermining her own party's maneuver.
content:
A motion of no confidence requested by George Miliband of the Jasmin Movement was swiftly dismantled on the floor today. Parliament, including members of the opposition, voiced significant support for Prime Minister Patrick Cutter, prioritizing institutional stability amid the escalating Myratian Crisis.

The vote comes at a highly volatile moment for Caprica. The Myratian Crisis—an armed uprising led by supporters of the Edelstein Political Dynasty—has gripped the nation following claims that the recent election was stolen by Matteo von Vralik of the United Party of Caprica. Tensions boiled over following the arrest of the dynasty's current leader, Dame Rachel Edelstein-Powell, prompting Edelsteinists to take up arms and demand an immediate by-election.

The political landscape was further rocked today by the court's highly anticipated ruling on Edelstein-Powell. While the court found her not guilty (9-0) on charges of insurrection and seditious conspiracy, she was found guilty in a narrow 5-4 decision on the charge of provocation of violence. She has been sentenced to six months in prison, to be served outside of Myrati.

It was against this explosive backdrop that Miliband attempted to topple the Cutter government. However, the opposition overwhelmingly rejected the maneuver, viewing a collapse of the government as an unacceptable risk while the Edelsteinist uprising remains active.

Further complicating the failed motion was a stunning display of internal division within the Jasmin Movement itself. Party chairman Jasmin was observed on the floor voting in favor of the government, explicitly breaking ranks and severely undermining Miliband's maneuver. As of this evening, there has been no public reaction or statement from Miliband regarding his chairman's defection.
byline: By Elsa Rourke, AVIS Politics Desk

headline: Local Man Discovers He's Been Paying Rent to a Pigeon for Three Years
summary: A startling revelation emerged in a downtown apartment complex today when a resident learned his elusive landlord, "Mr. Coo," was in fact a particularly enterprising rock dove nesting in the building's ventilation shaft. Legal experts remain divided on whether the pigeon is required to return the security deposit.
byline: By Nadia Voss, AVIS Society Desk
